Subject: Request: Trial bridge & credits — integration backlog

Hi Vivek,

Quick note from the Integrate.ai engineering team — our connector work for Redwood hit an unexpected blocker around our auth flow. The engineers estimate ~3 additional weeks to finish end-to-end testing. We were planning to complete before the trial expires, but now we risk losing momentum and the execs want to keep a live demo running for another month.

Can Redwood provide a 30-day trial extension and a small sandbox credit top-up to cover the additional token usage required for a live demo? If helpful, I attached our current integration timeline (integration_timeline.xlsx).

We’d like to keep the contract timeline intact (decision by 7/22) but need runway to finish the integration and run the demo with customers. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer.

Thanks —
Samir Shah
Dir, Platform Engineering
Integrate.ai

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the heads up and for sending the timeline. Sorry to hear about the auth blocker; appreciate the visibility.

I’ve looped in Neha (rev ops) and Diego (customer success) to evaluate a short trial extension + sandbox credit allocation. High level: we can usually approve a 30-day extension for integration blockers and a modest token credit grant for demo runway, but I need confirmation on the expected token burn and the exec ask. Can you add an estimate (tokens/day or expected API spend) and confirm whether the demo will be internal-only or customer-facing?

If you prefer, we can treat this as a Trial Bridge (internal name RDW-TRIAL-BRIDGE) and put standard bridge terms in a short DocuSign so your legal and ours have visibility. Diego — any initial thoughts on credits/precedent here?

Best,

Forwarding Samir’s request — thread below.

Quick summary: Integrate.ai asks for a 30-day trial extension + sandbox credit top-up to finish an auth integration. They expect to keep their decision timeline (7/22). Attachment includes a timeline.

Requesting approval for: 30-day extension + $2k equivalent in sandbox credits (covers demo burn). If we want to be conservative we can cap credits by token limits and require the DocuSign bridge terms (standard).

Why approve: Integrate.ai is a strategic mid-market account, platform-led purchase, with a likely annual ARR in the mid-six figures if we win. Losing live demo momentum increases churn risk.

If approved, I’ll send the DocuSign and confirm the credit allocation.

Proposed DocuSign language: 30-day authorization, one-time sandbox credit grant (non-refundable) tied to trial account RDW-INT-0891, audit logs retained.

Neha — can you confirm discount authority / who needs to sign off? Diego — CS to add acceptance criteria for the extension?

Thanks,
Vivek
